clue.text: Sad preliminary to dinner by the Limpopo ?

definitions.text: Sad preliminary to dinner by the Limpopo ?

parts.words: Sad preliminary to dinner by the Limpopo ?
parts.note: the great grey-green Limpopo of Kipling's Just So Stories teems with crocodiles, said to weep false tears as they eat their prey; the sadness before dinner is a pretence

explanation.surface: A gloomy aperitif before an evening meal on the banks of an African river.
explanation.walkthrough: The insincere grief is the reptile's, shed over the victim it is about to eat; the Limpopo is where Kipling's Elephant's Child met one.
explanation.definitionFit: Feigned sorrow is named after the reptile's supposed habit of weeping while devouring its prey.

clue.text: The senior officer's taking wine with the cavalryman

parts.note: CO is commanding officer, the senior officer, plus the possessive S
sack is an old name for dry white wine from Spain

explanation.surface: The colonel has a drink with a mounted trooper.
explanation.definitionFit: These Russian horsemen were famous light cavalry.

clue.text: "Not the least made" the raven

parts.note: the line in Poe's poem The Raven runs 'Not the least ... made he', the gap being the bird's lack of a bow

explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has a dash between 'least' and 'made': fill the gap in the line from Edgar Allan Poe's poem The Raven.
explanation.definitionFit: A deferential bow or gesture of respect, which the poem's bird pointedly fails to make.

clue.text: Source of wealth for the Beverly Hillbillies

definitions.text: Source of wealth for the Beverly Hillbillies

parts.words: Source of wealth for the Beverly Hillbillies
parts.note: in the American sitcom, the Clampett family get rich when crude bubbles up on their land while hunting

explanation.walkthrough: The Beverly Hillbillies was a 1960s American TV comedy about a poor mountain family made millionaires by a strike of crude.
explanation.definitionFit: A bore that pumps petroleum from underground is the family's gusher.

clue.text: Being so makes one scold

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
to rate someone is an old word for berating them

explanation.surface: Someone who scolds must be in that state already.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being so' is the definition, standing for the adjective; read the rest as I (one) plus RATE (scold).
explanation.definitionFit: Being angry is what drives a person to scold.

clue.text: Like chickens before they're hatched

parts.note: recalls the proverb about counting chickens before they hatch; inside the egg they are not yet fully formed

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb warns against counting on things before they exist; literally the chick is still a developing creature in the shell.
explanation.definitionFit: Describes something at an early, undeveloped stage, as a chick is in the egg.

clue.text: As dead as the dodo

parts.note: the flightless Mauritian bird was wiped out in the 17th century, so it is the standard image of a vanished species

explanation.definitionFit: A species that has died out entirely no longer survives anywhere.

clue.text: Diamond shape

parts.note: a parallelogram with four equal sides, the lozenge on a playing card

explanation.definitionFit: This geometric figure is a four-sided equilateral parallelogram, the outline of the card suit.

clue.text: Four points to the old Palestinian

parts.note: east is one compass point
south is a second compass point
south-east is a third compass point
north-east is a fourth compass point

explanation.surface: Directions given to an ancient traveller in the Holy Land.
explanation.walkthrough: Four compass points are E, S, SE and NE, together six letters; the answer is a member of an ascetic Jewish sect of Roman times.
explanation.definitionFit: This ascetic Jewish brotherhood flourished in Judea around the time of Christ.

clue.text: Fine and dandy

definitions.meaning: as an informal adjective, splendid or excellent
as a noun, a fashionably dressed man about town

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fine and dandy' reads as one stock phrase, but it splits into two senses: an adjective and a noun for a fop.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally the word means excellent, and as a noun it is an old term for a smartly dressed gentleman.

clue.text: Neckwear for an old man of the sea

definitions.text: Neckwear for an old man of the sea

parts.words: Neckwear for an old man of the sea
parts.note: in Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner the old sailor wears round his neck the great seabird he shot

explanation.surface: A tie or scarf suited to an elderly sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'old man of the sea' is Coleridge's Ancient Mariner, punished by having the dead bird hung about his neck instead of a cross.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird the mariner shot is hung round his neck as a mark of guilt, a burden now proverbial.

clue.text: Yet a rule's broken in no mild manner

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

parts.note: the word with its apostrophe dropped supplies the five letters R, U, L, E, S

explanation.surface: Nevertheless a regulation was breached in quite a harsh way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges YET, A and RULES (the apostrophe ignored) into the nine-letter adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with severity and sternness is the opposite of acting mildly.

clue.text: No French cereal for the aristocrat

parts.note: taken as written
blé is the French word for wheat or corn

explanation.surface: Turning down the Parisian breakfast grain offered to a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer or nobleman is a member of the aristocracy.

clue.text: Faineant monarch

parts.note: in Aesop's fable the frogs asked Jupiter for a ruler and were sent a log, which lay idle and did nothing

explanation.walkthrough: Fainéant means idle or do-nothing; Aesop's frogs found their wooden ruler so inert they begged for another and got a stork that ate them.
explanation.definitionFit: The fable's inert wooden ruler stands for any lazy, ineffectual leader.

clue.text: Might one describe him as the Thousand and First Italian Knight?

definitions.text: Might one describe him as the Thousand and First Italian Knight?

parts.words: Might one describe him as the Thousand and First Italian Knight?
parts.note: plays on the Arabian Nights' thousand and one tales and the Thousand, the red-shirted volunteers whom this general led to Sicily in 1860

explanation.walkthrough: 'Knight' puns on the Thousand and One Nights; the leader of the Expedition of the Thousand would be the one added on top.
explanation.definitionFit: This patriot general led the Expedition of the Thousand that helped unify Italy.

clue.text: Striking absence of furniture ?

parts.note: a lack of something is expressed as 'no' before it
a table is an item of furniture

explanation.surface: A room conspicuously bare of chairs and cupboards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Striking' looks like part of the description of the empty room, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something remarkable or conspicuous strikes the eye.

clue.text: No dead science, his

parts.note: the study he pursues is that of life, so it is the opposite of a dead subject

explanation.walkthrough: 'No dead science' looks like praise for a lively discipline, but literally it is the science of living things.
explanation.definitionFit: A scientist who studies living organisms works in the life sciences.

clue.text: Where the traveller strips again when retiring ?

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the word for stripping again is read backwards

parts.note: to peel a second time is to strip off once more

explanation.surface: A hotel room where a guest undresses once more before going to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when retiring' reverses REPEELS; the traveller here is on a night train, where he sleeps in a berth.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carriage with berths lets passengers sleep on an overnight journey.

clue.text: Where one can see strange apparitions

definitions.text: Where one can see strange apparitions

parts.words: Where one can see strange apparitions
parts.note: a meeting where a medium tries to contact spirits, which may appear to the sitters

explanation.definitionFit: Spiritualists gather at such a sitting hoping to summon the ghosts of the dead.

clue.text: A pious heraldic bird

parts.note: in heraldry the bird 'in her piety' is shown pecking her breast to feed her young on her blood

explanation.walkthrough: The heraldic device 'in her piety' shows the mother wounding herself for her brood, a symbol of Christ's sacrifice.
explanation.definitionFit: This large-billed waterbird was believed to nourish its chicks with its own blood, so it symbolises piety.

clue.text: Set sail — from the Needles ?

definitions.meaning: to untie a boat's moorings and depart
in knitting, to finish by taking the stitches off the needles

explanation.surface: A yacht leaving port past the Needles, chalk stacks off the Isle of Wight.
explanation.walkthrough: The Needles are chalk rocks off the Isle of Wight, a natural starting point for a voyage; the second sense is knitting.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both a boat freeing its lines and a knitter binding off the final row of stitches.

clue.text: Direction follows a sequence o notes with this triangle

indicators.note: follows places the compass direction after the run of notes

parts.note: a scale is a run of musical notes in order; the page lost the f of 'of'
NE is north-east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A musician's instructions for playing a triangle after the scale.
explanation.walkthrough: The triangle in the surface sounds like the percussion instrument, but the answer is a term from geometry.
explanation.definitionFit: A triangle with three unequal sides is called by this geometric term.

clue.text: Does this writer use an eyebrow pencil ?

definitions.text: Does this writer use an eyebrow pencil ?

parts.words: Does this writer use an eyebrow pencil ?
parts.note: a journalist who writes long magazine articles shares a name with a part of the face that make-up enhances

explanation.walkthrough: The writer is a journalist of long-form pieces; the eyebrow pencil suggests the other sense, a part of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a distinctive part of the face and a long newspaper article.

clue.text: Inspiring holy dread or vulgar distaste

definitions.meaning: in its old literal sense, full of reverent awe
in colloquial use, very bad or unpleasant

explanation.walkthrough: 'vulgar' here means popular or colloquial: the everyday usage of the word, not its archaic meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally the word meant filling one with reverent fear; casual speech now uses it for anything dreadful or nasty.

clue.text: The highest degree

parts.note: the top class of British university honours degree

explanation.walkthrough: British honours degrees are classed: the top grade beats an upper or lower second.
explanation.definitionFit: Graduates achieving top marks are awarded a first-class honours degree.

clue.text: Manager takes a new star to the dance

parts.note: a boss is the one in charge
a nova is a star that suddenly flares, Latin for new

explanation.surface: A theatre director escorts a fresh celebrity to the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: This Brazilian style blending samba and jazz is a popular ballroom dance.

clue.text: A bit of thieves' language

indicators.note: a bit is a small part, so a run of letters is taken from inside the following words

explanation.surface: A fragment of the criminal underworld's private jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A bit of' picks letters spanning the apostrophe, thieveS LANGuage; and thieves' cant is itself an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal or underworld vocabulary, such as criminals' cant, is a form of colloquial speech.

clue.text: Lynx-headed Emperor of Rome

parts.note: the name of the third-century emperor begins with the name of a desert lynx, the caracal

explanation.walkthrough: A caracal is a long-eared lynx of Africa and Asia; the emperor's name has that animal at its head.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the nickname of the emperor Marcus Aurelius Antoninus, who ruled Rome from 198 to 217.

clue.text: A Biblical character's French oil concoction

indicators.note: a concoction is something mixed together, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: huile is the French word for oil

explanation.surface: A scriptural figure's Gallic olive-oil recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction' rearranges HUILE, the French for oil. The answer is the young man who speaks to Job in the Book of Job.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Job this young man rebukes Job and his three comforters.

clue.text: It reacts dangerously to the gentle touch

definitions.text: It reacts dangerously to the gentle touch

parts.words: It reacts dangerously to the gentle touch
parts.note: a hedgerow plant whose hairs inject an irritant when brushed lightly, though grasping it firmly is said to be harmless

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says to grasp it boldly: tender handling is what gets you hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: This weed's hairs deliver a painful chemical sting to skin that brushes against them.
